subject: Cloud Computing
title: Disaster Recovery in the Cloud
description: Learn Disaster Recovery in the Cloud in one minute.

hook.text: A fire destroys your primary data center. Can your business survive? Cloud makes it possible.

buildup.text: Disaster recovery means keeping a standby copy of your entire system in a different location.

discovery.text: Cloud enables this cheaply. Replicate to another region and only activate it during a real disaster.

twist.text: Most companies never test their DR plans. When disaster strikes, they discover the backup is broken.

climax.text: The cloud makes disaster recovery affordable. Testing it regularly makes it actually work.

punchline.text: A backup plan is useless if you've never tested it.

quiz.question: What is the biggest mistake companies make with disaster recovery?
options: Having a recovery plan but never testing it
Spending too much money on redundant systems
Using cloud services instead of on-premises backups

details.summary: Cloud disaster recovery uses cross-region replication, automated failover, and infrastructure as code to restore services after catastrophic failures. Strategies range from simple backups in another region to fully active multi-region deployments, each balancing cost against recovery speed.
details.whyItMatters: Disaster recovery in the cloud is dramatically simpler and cheaper than with owned infrastructure. Understanding DR strategies helps design appropriate protection for your recovery objectives.
takeaways: DR strategies range from backup-restore to active-active multi-region
RTO and RPO define recovery speed and acceptable data loss
Infrastructure as code makes environment recreation automated

faq.question: What are RTO and RPO?
faq.answer: Recovery Time Objective is the maximum acceptable time to restore service after a disaster. Recovery Point Objective is the maximum acceptable data loss measured in time. An RPO of one hour means you can lose up to one hour of data. These define your DR strategy and cost.

faq.question: What are the main DR strategies?
faq.answer: Backup and restore is cheapest but slowest. Pilot light keeps minimal infrastructure running in the DR region. Warm standby runs a scaled-down copy. Active-active runs full capacity in multiple regions simultaneously, offering near-zero RTO and RPO but at the highest cost.
